prerequisites: Expression through written and oral communication in technical language of the theoretical fundamentals in the field of engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Explains the fundamental principles of thermodynamics applied to compressible fluids, including isentropic relations, state equations, and wave phenomena.
Describes compressible flow regimes and the subsonic-transonic-supersonic transition criteria.
Identifies and applies conservation equations (mass, momentum, energy) in the analysis of jets, diffusers, nozzles, and convergent-divergent nozzles.
Explains the mechanisms of shock wave formation and propagation, and expansion waves.
Integrates thermodynamic efficiency concepts in the analysis of turbomachinery and propulsion systems.
Uses characteristic maps, thermodynamic diagrams, and numerical models to describe the behavior of compressible fluids.
Models compressible flow processes using analytical, graphical, and numerical methods.
Applies engineering calculation methods in sizing nozzles, diffusers, combustion chambers, and other components with compressible flow.
Experimentally interprets parameters such as Mach number, total pressure, static pressure, total temperature, and sonic velocity.
Uses specialized software for CFD analysis and simulations of compressible flows.
Solves specific engineering problems in the field, formulating appropriate hypotheses and evaluating solution sensitivity.
Respects professional ethics and safety norms in handling equipment for aerodynamic parameter measurement.
Integrates into multidisciplinary technical teams involved in the design or operation of systems with compressible flows.
Demonstrates autonomy in specialized documentation, using updated scientific sources.
Develops engineering projects in the field of energy and propulsion systems, adopting efficient, sustainable, and safe solutions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to thermodynamics of compressible fluids: properties, state equations, sonic velocity, Mach number
Conservation equations for compressible flows: mass, momentum, energy; isentropic flow
Flow regimes: subsonic, transonic, supersonic; effect of compressibility on fluid parameters
Flow through convergent and convergent-divergent nozzles; critical flow; normal shock
Oblique shock waves, normal shocks, Rankine-Hugoniot relations; Prandtl-Meyer expansion waves
Flow in pipes with friction and without friction: Fanno model and Rayleigh model
Applications in mechanical engineering: turbomachinery, compressors, propulsion systems, pneumatic installations.
State equations for compressible gases. Calculation of air parameters
Determination of sonic velocity and Mach number
Isentropic flow: pressure, temperature, density ratios
Critical flow and sonic condition in convergent nozzles
Convergent-divergent nozzle: determination of state in sections
Applications in turbomachinery: compressors and turbines
CFD software and interpretation of results for compressible flows
Defining the project topic and engineering scope
Bibliographic study and technical documentation
Theoretical modeling of the analyzed system
Numerical calculation of thermodynamic states and flow parameters
CFD numerical simulation (optional / recommended)
Interpretation of results and evaluation of system performance
Final drafting and project presentation
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with emphasis on connections between theoretical modeling and engineering applications
PowerPoint presentations, containing graphics, diagrams, constructive schemes, and experimental examples
Discovery-based concept development (deductions, modeling, scenario analysis), supported by numerical demonstrations and exercises
Problem-solving and engineering applications, oriented towards turbomachinery behavior and flow in nozzles
Continuous correlation of theoretical phenomena with real applications in aerodynamics, energetics, and fluid mechanics
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the weighted scores of each activity within the discipline. Grades are awarded from 1 to 10, with a minimum grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. A minimum grade of 5 is required for each of the major components (Exam, Laboratory, Project).
